root.name: salvor
root.about: Salvor CLI: run, resume, list, history, and replay for durable agent runs

args.help: Path to the SQLite event store

subcommands.name: run
subcommands.about: Start a fresh run of an agent

args.help: Path to the agent definition (TOML). Required unless `--fixture` is given, which supplies the agent itself
The run input: a JSON value, or `@path` to read JSON from a file. Required unless `--fixture` is given, which supplies the input itself
Run a self-contained fixture directory offline: no API key, no network

subcommands.name: resume
subcommands.about: Continue an existing run: resume a parked one, or recover a crashed one

args.help: The run id (a UUID) to continue
Path to an agent definition (TOML), needed to rebuild the agent. Repeatable: an agent run needs exactly one; a graph run needs the files its `agent` nodes reference (zero or more)

Path to the graph document (JSON), needed to re-drive a GRAPH run. The run's log records only the graph's hash, not the document, exactly as it records an agent by hash and not its definition; so a graph run's resume re-supplies the document here, the same way an agent run re-supplies its definition through `--agent`. Its hash must match the one the run recorded. Omit for an ordinary agent run
The resume input, required for a parked run: a JSON value, or `@path`. Ignored (with a warning) when recovering a crashed run

subcommands.name: fork
subcommands.about: Fork a graph run from a node boundary into a NEW run, refusing to re-execute a recorded write the operator has not acknowledged

args.help: The origin run id (a UUID) to fork
The node boundary to restart the fork from: the fork re-walks from this node, carrying the origin's events below it as an identical prefix

Path to the graph document (JSON) the origin ran. Re-supplied the same way a graph resume re-supplies it (the log records only the hash); its hash must match the recorded one, since a fork reuses the origin's graph unchanged
An agent definition (TOML) the graph's `agent` nodes reference. Repeatable, exactly as `graph run` and a graph `resume` take them

Acknowledge the writes the re-walked segment would re-fire: a comma-separated list of origin log positions (`4,7`), or `all` to acknowledge the full hazard set. Recorded permanently into the child's fork origin. Omit when the fork boundary sits before any write
Print what the fork WOULD do (the hazard list and the would-be prefix summary) without creating a run

subcommands.name: resolve
subcommands.about: Record the completion of a dangling write by hand, after verifying it

args.help: The run id (a UUID) that needs reconciliation

The output to record for the dangling write, after verifying externally what it did: a JSON value, or `@path` to read JSON from a file. It is recorded verbatim as the tool's output, so replay never re-runs the write

subcommands.name: abandon
subcommands.about: Abandon a run: retire it by hand without finishing or failing it, for a run that is dead forever or no longer worth carrying

args.help: The run id (a UUID) to abandon
An optional note for why the run is being abandoned, recorded on the terminal event. Omit it to abandon with no reason

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.about: List runs in the store, newest activity last. Filters narrow what is printed; with none, every run is listed

args.help: Keep only runs with this status. Repeatable; a run matching ANY of them is kept. Values are the labels the STATUS column prints. To filter by a whole group of states instead, use `--group`

Keep only runs in this group: `waiting` (needs a person), `progress` (moving on its own), or `terminal` (finished, one way or another). These are the same three groups the status colours use. To filter by a single state instead, use `--status`
Keep only runs whose agent identity contains this text: a definition hash, or `graph run` for a graph
Print at most N runs, keeping the most recently active ones. The order on screen is unchanged, so the newest still sit at the bottom

subcommands.name: completions
subcommands.about: Print a shell completion script for `salvor` on stdout

args.help: The shell to generate for
The run id (a UUID) whose log to print
Print the raw event envelopes as JSON instead of the pretty log

subcommands.name: replay
subcommands.about: Re-derive a run's state from its log without executing anything

args.help: The run id (a UUID) to re-derive state for
Re-derive state from the log without executing anything. Required in this version: live replay is not yet available

subcommands.name: serve
subcommands.about: Run the control-plane HTTP + server-sent-events server over the store

args.help: The address to bind, host and port

The NAME of an environment variable holding a shared-secret bearer token. When set (and the variable is non-empty), every request must carry `Authorization: Bearer <that value>`. When omitted, the server runs without auth, trusting a reverse proxy to guard it. Never the token itself, matching how agent files name key variables

Kill the running `salvor serve` instead of serving. With no value, discovers every running `salvor serve` (by inspecting the process table, since there are no pid files): zero found is reported and this exits; exactly one is killed; multiple print a numbered table and prompt for a choice. Given a value (a pid or a listening port), kills that one directly with no prompt. When present at all, this short-circuits before `--bind` or `--store` are acted on: the process never binds a port

Also start the Angular dev server (`ng serve`) for `bridge/`, hot module reloading included, with `/v1` proxied to this API so a browser at the dev server's own URL calls straight through. This process's own bind/store handling is otherwise unchanged: the API binds and serves exactly as plain `serve` does. Requires a salvor checkout with a `bridge/` directory alongside it; the dashboard an installed `salvor` embeds is prebuilt and does not hot-reload
Register a small set of deterministic demo tools (`lookup_invoice` read, `issue_refund` write, `send_email` idempotent) instead of the stock empty tool registry

subcommands.name: build
subcommands.about: Build the whole product from a salvor checkout: the web dashboard, then the release binary that embeds it

args.help: After building, install the release binary onto the PATH with `cargo install --path crates/salvor-cli`, so the `salvor` you run from anywhere carries the dashboard just built

subcommands.name: graph
subcommands.about: Author-time graph document tools: validate a document, or print its JSON Schema. These read no store and drive no run

subcommands.name: validate
subcommands.about: Validate a graph document JSON file: parse it strictly and run every check, printing a summary on success or the precise node/edge errors on failure

args.help: Path to the graph document (JSON)

subcommands.name: schema
subcommands.about: Print the graph document JSON Schema to stdout

subcommands.name: run
subcommands.about: Drive a graph document locally over the store, exactly as `salvor run` drives an agent run: each `agent` node resolves to a provided `--agent` file (keyed by its computed definition hash), and each `tool` node resolves from the tools those agents carry

args.help: Path to the graph document (JSON)
The run input: a JSON value, or `@path` to read JSON from a file

An agent definition (TOML) an `agent` node may reference. Repeatable: each file is built and keyed by its computed definition hash, and a graph `agent_hash` that matches none of them fails with a precise message listing the hashes that were provided
A correlation tag `key=value`, recorded once on the run's `GraphRunStarted`. Repeatable
